    The decomposition theorem #

    Every finite-dimensional module over a string algebra is a finite direct product of string and band modules (exists_decomposition).

    For each orbit of nonzero pairs we take one realization: a string or band module X with a map to M inducing isomorphisms of the pair functors at all positions (Piece). By the position counts, the pair functors of the product of the pieces have the same dimensions as those of M; the dimension formula gives equal dimensions, and the spanning lemma gives surjectivity.

    source
    theorem BrickAccessibility.MonomialData.finrank_eq_sum_vsp {k : Type u} [Field k] {B : Type u} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] {D : MonomialData k B} (M : Type u_1) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module k M] [IsScalarTower k B M] [FiniteDimensional k M] :
    Module.finrank k M = ∑ v : D.Q.V, Module.finrank k ↥(D.vsp M v)

    A module is the direct sum of its vertex spaces.
